quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 results (CFO Jayshree Desai): for the full year, revenues reached $28.5 billion, an increase of 20% compared to 2024; adjusted EBITDA was a record $2.9 billion and adjusted diluted EPS grew 20% year-over-year to $10.75; record cash flow from operations of $2.2 billion and record free cash flow of $1.7 billion. Fourth-quarter revenues were $7.8 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of $845 million and adjusted diluted EPS of $3.16, all records; Q4 free cash flow was $946 million, a fourth-quarter record. Duke Austin: record revenues 8 of the last 9 years, 8 consecutive years of record adjusted EBITDA and 9 consecutive years of record adjusted diluted EPS.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenues $28.5 billion (an increase of 20%); adjusted EBITDA $2.9 billion; adjusted diluted EPS $10.75 (grew 20%); cash flow from operations $2.2 billion; free cash flow $1.7 billion; Q4 revenues $7.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA $845 million, adjusted diluted EPS $3.16, free cash flow $946 million

quarterly_data.signal: Initial FY2026 outlook (CFO Jayshree Desai): continued double-digit growth in revenues, net income and adjusted EBITDA and 'the opportunity to deliver over 20% growth in adjusted EPS', supported by the record year-end backlog; free cash flow of $1.8 billion at the midpoint, which includes $250 million to $350 million of capital expenditures for the vertical supply chain solution and contemplates collecting the remaining balance on the large Canadian renewable transmission project. Duke Austin: 2026 is 'really just solid growth across a broad spectrum of markets' with no 765 type work starting and no major large projects; SunZia 'is really not going to move the needle' with 'the company at $33.5 billion'. Asked about an analyst's 10.3% Electric margin midpoint, he said Quanta 'took a prudent approach to the midpoint of the guidance' and has opportunity to improve, but organic hiring pressures margins and 50% plus of the business is regulated, so 'it's really a compounding story'.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026: double-digit growth in revenues, net income and adjusted EBITDA; over 20% growth in adjusted EPS; free cash flow $1.8 billion at the midpoint, including $250 million to $350 million of vertical-supply-chain capex; 'the company at $33.5 billion' (SunZia 'not going to move the needle')

quarterly_data.signal: VERTICAL SUPPLY CHAIN ANNOUNCED FOR TRANSFORMERS AND BREAKERS (Duke Austin): Quanta is 'strategically investing approximately $500 million to $700 million over the next several years in our power transformer manufacturing facilities and vertical supply chain strategy. The majority of this investment will build out production for the 345-kilovolt through 765-kilovolt power transformers and breakers', which he expects to be a significant differentiated solution in the high-voltage transmission market. In Q&A he framed it as de-risking: '$300 million to $500 million, probably up in the $700 million over the next 3 years is derisking us. The transformers breakers, the things that we're building don't show up, we have issues, significant issues.' Customer discussions center on 'labor constraints, vertical supply chain issues'. Quanta has not taken outside money for its expansions although it has 'been offered on transformers'. CFO: $250 million to $350 million of 2026 capital expenditures relate to this vertical supply chain solution.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $500 million to $700 million over the next several years in power transformer manufacturing and vertical supply chain; majority for 345-kilovolt through 765-kilovolt power transformers and breakers; $250 million to $350 million of expected 2026 capital expenditures related to the vertical supply chain solution

quarterly_data.signal: Data center / technology end market (Duke Austin): data center is 'roughly like 10% of the business at this point', and its backlog 'is certainly growing. It's our fastest-growing piece of backlog'; he expects to keep 'booking significant backlog this year and beyond' and sees 'at least a decade of growth in that area'. Quanta now plays in two verticals - 'the technology TAM that's well over $1 trillion and the utility TAM over $1 trillion and growing' - and is working with technology customers toward more programmatic spend. The Q3 acquisition of Dynamic Systems, a turnkey mechanical and process infrastructure provider, strengthens its presence in technology, semiconductor, health care and load center markets. Quanta will not put capital into data-center assets: 'if you invest significantly with co-locator hyperscaler and things that like that, you run the risk of competing with who our client is and we don't do that.'
quarterly_data.figure: data center roughly like 10% of the business; fastest-growing piece of backlog; technology TAM well over $1 trillion and utility TAM over $1 trillion

quarterly_data.signal: DC power architecture for data centers (an analyst asked about the shift from 54-volt to 800-volt DC): Duke Austin - 'voltage going to DC, some of the architecture that NVIDIA has put out ... I believe we're in front of that I don't see it changing our TAM at all. You might get more medium voltage type arrangements in there. Still a lot of low voltage type things.' 'We work with NVIDIA and others to make sure that we see where they're going and make sure we have the craft necessary.' Older architecture will still be used and 'both are growing significantly'. Front vs behind the meter: it is better to let the utility take the chips' intermittency, but 'People are trying to go behind the meter simply because you can't get to the meter' because of queue constraints; he expects much off-grid generation to become backup power ('you'll start with 100, 200 max and then back up for a bit and then come on with utility type solutions'). Quanta never left natural gas and is getting involved in plants 'backing up some of the hyperscalers and data centers'.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (DC power architecture not expected to change Quanta's TAM; more medium voltage arrangements possible)

quarterly_data.signal: GAS GENERATION PLATFORM (Duke Austin): in October Quanta was selected by NiSource 'to design, procure and construct generation and infrastructure resources, capable of producing approximately 3 gigawatts of power for our large data center campus in Indiana'; he said the Indiana project amounts to a '$7 a month rebate basically to every rate payer in NiSource, maybe more'. Customers are asking Quanta to build combined cycles, single cycles and all types of generation - 'There is no shortage of inbound calls when in Quanta to build generation.' It will book generation both in JV settings and alone, always risk-adjusted, with no firm fixed price generation. 'So the first one is not in backlog. I suspect we'll have multiple in backlog before the end of the year. And I think it's more of a '27, '28, '29 type build, where that's the ramp on it'.
quarterly_data.figure: NiSource selection for approximately 3 gigawatts of generation for a large data center campus in Indiana; first generation project not in backlog; multiple expected in backlog before year-end; '27, '28, '29 type build

quarterly_data.signal: Large transmission timing and contracting (Duke Austin): 'we have no significant 765, no 765, which I consider those large projects in the backlog'; in 2026 'we don't anticipate starting any 765 type work' and the 765 initiatives are 'not in backlog yet'. 'I think you'll see us book later half of 2027, a significant amount of 765 and other types of work. It's not just 765, it's 345, 500. Data centers, I don't know, generation, it's stacking. I feel confident that there will be some chunky awards all the way through the next 3 to 5 years.' Contracting has shifted from bidding 1-year and 2-year work: 'Now we're not bidding at all. We're negotiating 5, 10-year type programmatic spend.' Demand: 'I don't see any demand slowdown at all'; 'we're probably in 2032 now kind of looking at things and booking things.' Renewables keep double-digit growth with visibility through 2030 ('booking through', not booked out); solar and batteries are 'the very fastest thing we can put on the grid right now in many areas'.
quarterly_data.figure: no significant 765, no 765 in backlog; no 765 type work starting in 2026; significant 765 bookings expected later half of 2027; chunky awards through the next 3 to 5 years; negotiating 5, 10-year type programmatic spend

quarterly_data.signal: Craft labour (Duke Austin): acquisitions plus organic growth added approximately 11,100 employees in 2025, bringing the workforce to approximately 69,500 at year-end; organically 'we'll grow around 6,000 employees', which pressures margins. On tightness: 'it's across the board' and 'it is tight. I would say anything around the data center stuff is probably the tightest market at this point. The utility type transmission, big transmission, things like that hasn't really started yet. You'll see that in the back half.' Distribution is modest growth; in telecom 'you'll start to see fiber splicers, things like that get tight.' 'Any time you have a tight craft labor market, Quanta does very well.'
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 69,500 employees at year-end (approximately 11,100 added in 2025 including acquisitions); organically will grow around 6,000 employees; data center work is the tightest craft market

quarterly_data.signal: M&A and prefab capacity: Quanta completed 8 acquisitions in 2025, including Dynamic Systems in Q3; in Q4 it closed Tri-City Group, Wilson Construction Company and Billings Flying Service for aggregate upfront consideration of approximately $1.7 billion in cash and Quanta common stock (CFO Jayshree Desai), expanding power delivery capabilities for large load center facilities and utility capital programs, while keeping the leverage ratio below 2x. Duke Austin: Tri-City brought custom fabrication capability that 'just adds to the 3 million square feet we already have' ('We call it premanufactured because it is manufactured'); Cupertino was the first mover in prefab over a decade ago, 'we're certainly willing to fab for others', and 'there's no shortage of people willing to shore up capacity for 3-, 5-decade type arrangement.'
quarterly_data.figure: 8 acquisitions in 2025; Q4 acquisitions approximately $1.7 billion upfront; leverage ratio below 2x; Tri-City fab capabilities add to the 3 million square feet of fabrication Quanta already has
